ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Focused Visit (Follow-up) — Josephine Baker — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.originalText: Four-week review after the change to clopidogrel: breathlessness, blood pressure, potassium and kidney function, and cardiac rehabilitation

text.paragraph: Four-week review after the change to clopidogrel. [S]

Ms. Baker returns four weeks after ticagrelor was changed to clopidogrel. She took the loading dose as written, and within a week the episodes of air hunger stopped. She has completed ten cardiac rehabilitation sessions, now walks on the treadmill for 30 minutes at a brisk pace, and has begun light stretching and dance steps with the physiotherapist's approval. Her home blood pressure averages 124/76 on lisinopril 10 mg. She did not have the blood tests ordered for one to two weeks after the last visit (potassium, creatinine and lipids): the order went to the clinic laboratory, and she did not have a ride on the days it was open. She has had no lightheadedness, cough or bleeding. She met the social worker, who is helping her plan the repayment of her debts. She feels more like herself. [S]

Follow-up: Twelve-week review in eight weeks with an exercise test, a lipid panel and a PHQ-9, drawn and done at the rehabilitation center where possible.
